newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Buenos Aires power generation bid too low - source.
newsitem.headline: Buenos Aires power generation bid too low - source.

text.p: A consortium headed by Italy's Camuzzi was the only bidder for the generating unit of Buenos Aires electric firm ESEBA and Governor Eduardo Duhalde will be advised to declare it void, an ESEBA official told Reuters Monday.

The $19.7 million bid by the Sodigen consortium is considered too low and Buenos Aires province Public Works Minister Hugo Toledo will advise Duhalde this week to declare the tender void, the source said.

After selling earlier this month the distribution business of ESEBA for $1.1 billion, more than it had expected, Buenos Aires government officials said they saw the generation sector going for more than the $100 million technicians had initially estimated.
The provincial government could call another tender, the company official said.
The other firm that qualified for ESEBA's generation units was Argentine thermoelectric generator Central Costanera, but it did not show up at Monday's tender.
Central Costanera is 51 percent owned by Chile's ENDESA, controlled in turn by Chile's ENERSIS SA.
Camuzzi is part of another consortium -- Inversora Electrica de Buenos Aires -- that last week won ESEBA's distribution business in the Atlantic coast with a $404 million bid.

Camuzzi's partners in the group are United Utilities Plc -- a U.K. electricity firm --, Argentine cement producer Loma Negra and also local CEI Citicorp Holdings SA. CEI is almost 40 percent indirectly owned by Citibank.
No other details were immediately available.
